correctness.rationale: For 0<m<=1 both affine compositions are bounded by radial subadditivity, and the bounded multiplier criterion plus Liouville forces a constant. At m=2 a Gaussian complete square forces and verifies the unique exponential weight and norm. At 1<m<2 the reproducing kernel necessary estimate bounds the weight on one half-plane and permits suborder-one growth on its complement; half-plane Phragmen-Lindelof and Liouville rule out nonzero weights. At m>2 the positive m^2|b|^2 R^(m-2)/4 circular mean of the radial defect contradicts Jensen’s lower bound on a nonzero entire weight. Limits, endpoint conditions, and zero operator are explicitly treated.

value.rationale: The classification solves a natural existence question: whether a nonzero entire weight can rescue a borderline unit-slope translation, with sharp exponent regimes and a unique isolated Gaussian exception above one. It yields automatic invertibility in all surviving cases and exposes two genuinely different analytic obstructions for 1<m<2 and m>2, going beyond a supplied pointwise test or trivial exercise.
